name: Naantali
title: Naantali Ship Gauging | UTM for Tankers and Ice-Class Ships
description: Ultrasonic thickness gauging at Naantali: ice-class tankers at the oil harbour, ro-pax ferries and bulk carriers, plus gauging ahead of docking on Luonnonmaa.
h1: Ice-Class and Tanker Thickness Measurement at the Port of Naantali
intro: Naantali sits on a sheltered inlet of the Archipelago Sea west of Turku, and its harbour is built around an oil refinery, a ro-pax link to Sweden and a repair yard on the neighbouring island. Ice-class tankers and Baltic ferries pass through all winter, and their ice belts take the wear. Atlantis does not keep staff in Finland: we send technicians from India to the vessel, scheduled around the cargo operation or the yard slot.
keywords: ice class tanker ice belt gauging
product tanker ballast tank gauging finland

highlights.h: Ice belt wear before and after winter
highlights.p: Ships that trade into the northern Baltic wear their shell plating along the ice belt faster than anywhere else. Readings taken at Naantali before the season and again after it show exactly how much steel the winter used.

highlights.h: A refinery harbour for tanker work
highlights.p: Product tankers load at the oil harbour next to the refinery. Deck, piping and gas-free ballast tank gauging fits the cargo programme, and the results are ready for charterers' vetting inspectors.

highlights.h: A yard on the next island
highlights.p: The repair yard on Luonnonmaa has docks that take ships of this region. Gauging at the berth in Naantali lets the owner order steel before the ship goes in, so dock days are not lost waiting for plate.

port.h: Naantali and the approach through the archipelago
p: Naantali lies on the south-west coast of Finland, a short distance west of Turku, at the mainland edge of the Archipelago Sea. Ships coming from the Baltic follow a marked fairway between islands and skerries, with a pilot on board, and reach the harbour through channels that are narrow but deep. The town is a well-known holiday resort in summer, with a historic old centre and a visitor attraction on an island offshore, yet the working harbour a few kilometres away is a quite different place, dominated by the refinery and its tank farm.

The port handles oil and petroleum products in large volumes, dry bulk cargoes at separate quays, and a regular ro-pax connection to Kapellskär in Sweden. Product tankers range from small coastal ships to larger vessels with ice class, since Naantali exports to ports around the Baltic through the winter. Ferries and ro-ro vessels run on a fixed rotation. Because the refinery supplies much of Finland's fuel, tanker calls are frequent and often reliable in timing, which helps when a gauging scope needs to be planned a few days ahead.

Winter shapes the year. From about January to March the fairway can carry ice, icebreakers keep the channels open, and ships entering the port are expected to meet the ice-class requirements set by the Finnish and Swedish authorities. Ice damage and abrasion show up at the bow, along the waterline and at the plating behind the ice belt. Summer brings pleasant weather and light traffic from leisure craft, but also longer daylight for work on open decks, and the autumn gales can be the main weather limit for launch work.

facilities.h: Where gauging is done at and near Naantali
p: At the oil harbour a product tanker is alongside for the length of her loading or discharge, and the realistic scope is the deck, cargo-line supports, ballast tanks that the crew have emptied and ventilated, and the pump room, subject to the terminal's permit rules. At the ro-pax berth, work is confined to the ship's turnaround, so scopes are staged over several calls. Dry bulk quays give hold access after discharge, which is the right time for frames and hopper plating.

Naantali's repair yard sits on Luonnonmaa island, close to the harbour, with a drydock and a floating dock that serve ships of the Baltic and the Gulf of Finland. A ship that docks there can be gauged in the dock for renewal survey, but the more economical sequence is often to take readings alongside a few weeks earlier, so the yard receives a complete steel list with the booking. The same technique applies to ships that dock at other yards in Finland, Estonia or Poland.
list: Oil harbour berths — deck plating, cargo-line supports, pump room piping and gas-free ballast tanks on product tankers.
Ro-pax berth — vehicle decks, ramps, fire main and sea-water piping on the Sweden-route ferry during turnarounds.
Dry bulk quays — hold frames, tank tops, hopper plating and coamings on bulk carriers after discharge.
Luonnonmaa repair yard — in-dock gauging for renewal surveys and verification of readings taken afloat.
Archipelago Sea anchorages — launch-borne scopes for ships waiting for a berth or the pilot station.
Yards in Turku, Tallinn and Gdańsk — alternative dockings, planned from Naantali readings.

context.h: Traficom, ice class and the Finnish winter
p: Port state control in Finland is part of the Paris MoU system and is carried out by inspectors from the Finnish Transport and Communications Agency, Traficom. Tankers, ro-pax ferries and bulk carriers are all in the regime's targeting, and a ship with a poor record or a recent detention should expect early inspection. Ro-pax operators on regular Baltic routes are also subject to the EU directive on inspection of ro-ro passenger ships, which makes structure around doors and ramps, fire mains and bilge systems subjects of regular attention.

Finland applies winter navigation restrictions each season: ships calling at Finnish ports in ice conditions must meet minimum ice-class and engine-power requirements, which are set according to the severity of the ice. Ice-class ships carry thicker plating and extra framing along the ice belt, and the belt wears from repeated contact with ice and from abrasion. Owners schedule gauging of this area before and after the winter to track wastage, plan renewal and support survey decisions. The EU Ship Recycling Regulation, the emissions trading scheme and FuelEU Maritime apply to ships on these routes too.

jobs.p: Work at Naantali follows the winter cycle and the refinery's tanker traffic. We agree a scope with the superintendent, check the cargo or ferry schedule with the agent, and ask the crew to prepare tanks and voids where they can. Where the ship is bound for a yard, we arrange the readings so that they can be passed straight to the planner and the attending surveyor.
list: Ice-belt plating and frame gauging from inside wing ballast tanks on an ice-class product tanker before the winter season.
Post-winter repeat gauging of the same ice-belt strip, to compare with the autumn readings and set a renewal plan.
Deck plating, cargo-line support and ballast tank gauging on a tanker at the oil harbour ahead of a charterer's vetting inspection.
Vehicle-deck, ramp and fire-main piping readings on a Sweden-route ro-pax during repeated turnarounds.
Pre-docking steel estimate on a coaster before entering the Luonnonmaa yard.

logistics: Teams normally arrive at Turku Airport or at Helsinki-Vantaa and continue by road or rail towards Naantali; Turku is the closer option, with Helsinki offering more flight connections. Finland is a Schengen state, so technicians from India need Schengen visas and should apply well ahead. Access to the oil harbour and the ferry berth is controlled by the port and the terminal, and the ship's agent arranges passes, launches for the anchorage and communication with the pilots.

faqs.q: Can you gauge an ice-class ship's ice belt at Naantali?
faqs.a: Yes. We measure the shell plating strip along the ice belt and the framing behind it, from inside the wing ballast tanks once they are empty and ventilated. Doing it before winter and again after gives the owner a record of how much steel the season consumed and a basis for deciding between renewal now or at the next docking.

faqs.q: Is a drydock available at Naantali for a renewal survey?
faqs.a: Yes, the repair yard on Luonnonmaa has a drydock and a floating dock, and ships of the region are docked there regularly. We can gauge in the dock for the survey, or take readings at the berth beforehand so the yard receives a steel list when the ship is booked, which usually shortens the time spent in dock.

faqs.q: Can tanks on a tanker at the oil harbour be entered during loading?
faqs.a: Cargo tanks cannot, and ballast tanks only if they are empty, ventilated, gas-tested and covered by the terminal's permit. We plan deck plating, piping and ballast tanks around the cargo programme and agree with the master which spaces will be ready. Cargo tank structure is better dealt with at a cleaning stop or in the yard.

faqs.q: Does winter ice prevent gauging at Naantali?
faqs.a: Ice may delay a ship's arrival and slow pilot boats, but the harbour itself is kept open by icebreakers and work inside tanks and engine rooms is not affected. Open-deck scopes become harder in frost, so the team brings suitable gear and plans the outdoor readings for the middle of the day. The agent keeps us informed about arrival times.
